Article Title: HCLTech jumps over 7%, TCS up 5%: Why are IT stocks rallying
Article Text:
IT stocks jump 5%

Why are IT stocks rallying?

Inflation, crude prices remain top concerns

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

Dalal Street began Tuesday on a strong note, with tech-heavy stocks fuelling the gains and pushing the BSE Focused IT index and Nifty IT around 3% higher. HCLTech emerged as the top gainer, rising 7.11% to 1306.80 after reporting strong quarterly results a day earlier, backed by improved profitability metrics.Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), India's largest IT company, also gained 5.69% to 2248.00 after announcing a 15% rise in net profit in its quarterly earnings last week. Other IT stocks joined the rally, with Tech Mahindra climbing 3.52% to Rs 1,521.70 and Infosys rising 2.06% to Rs 1,038.Around 10:55 am, the Nifty IT index was up 3.12%, or 885.65 points, at 29,235.25, while the BSE Focused IT index had gained 3.04%, or 1,044.37 points, to 35,366.87. The broader market also traded higher, with BSE Sensex rising 466.15 points, or 0.65%, to 72,390.83. Nifty 50 was up 145.30 points, or 0.65%, at 22,508.65.Better-than-expected quarterly results from major IT companies have encouraged investors to return to beaten-down shares, raising hopes that concerns over the sector's earnings growth may be easing.Dharmesh Kant, head of equity research at Cholamandalam Securities, told Reuters, "The quarterly numbers reported by Accenture, TCS, and HCLTech indicate that the worst of earnings growth concerns for IT companies might be behind us.This is triggering a value buying opportunity in the sector."Despite Tuesday's rally, IT stocks have had a difficult year.The Nifty IT index has fallen 23% year-to-date amid moderating earnings growth and concerns about artificial intelligence disrupting traditional software services businesses.Rupee's recovery provided further support to market sentiment. The currency strengthened to 95.25 against the dollar after the Reserve Bank of India announced additional measures to ease pressure on the domestic currency.Investors are also keeping a close watch on the interest rate outlook after retail inflation accelerated to a higher-than-expected 5.54% in September. The latest reading has put the Reserve Bank of India's rate decisions in focus.Crude oil prices remain another concern. Brent crude futures fell by more than 1% during the day but continued to trade above $100 per barrel. Persistently high oil prices have fuelled inflation worries, particularly amid a weak monsoon.While domestic IT stocks advanced, global technology shares faced pressure following reports of rapid technological advances by Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies.The developments triggered a global sell-off in chipmakers, with South Korea's technology-heavy Kospi falling 6%. An index tracking Asian shares excluding Japan declined by more than 2%.
Article Summary: HCLTech emerged as the top gainer, rising 7.11% to 1306.80. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), India's largest IT company, also gained 5.69% to 2248.00. Despite Tuesday's rally, IT stocks have had a difficult year.

today:

On October 12, spot gold surrendered its gains made in the Asian session to slide lower as the day wore on as oil prices and Dollar Index strengthened.At the time of writing this article on the night of October 12, spot gold was changing hands at $4165, down nearly 0.7% for the day. Losses in domestic gold prices were more pronounced, down 1.3%, due to strong appreciation in the INR on significant steps taken by the RBI to support the ailing currency in the weekend.In the week ending October 9, the shiny metal closed with a weekly gain of 1.2% at $4194, though return of Chinese buyers after a week-long ‘golden week holiday’ helped the metal cushion its losses.A weekend attack on Saudi's Riyadh Airport on Saturday left 12 people dead, including an American, and over 300 injured. Saudi Arabia said it was dealing with missiles and drone attacks Monday also. The US President Trump said he is weighing joining war against the Houthis.The conflict between the Houthis and Yemen’s internationally recognised government, backed by Saudi Arabia, has intensified regional geopolitical tensions.Houthi attacks on Riyadh and the resulting aviation disruptions have affected the ongoing World Petroleum Congress, prompting several senior oil executives to withdraw from in-person participation, although the event is proceeding as planned. Attention will subsequently shift to the Future Investment Initiative, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s flagship investment conference, scheduled for October 26-29. Given the prominence of these events and continued Houthi warnings concerning Saudi airspace, the risk of further attacks is likely to remain elevated.Trump’s announcement of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine does not seem to be holding.Trump, through a social media post claimed that Russia has agreed to sell US diesel to the tune of 4.8 million tons in the coming months. Russia has not specified either dates or volumes. The initial tranche of 5,00,000 tons (125,000 bpd if spread across November) will be less than 10% of the diesel loss of 1.6 mbpd. The US consumes around 3.5-4 mb diesel/day. Even 4.8 million tons, promised to be delivered by the start of the next year, amount to merely 36 mb, well short of the US consumption.At the time of writing, Brent oil futures were trading with a daily gain of 2% at $106.75.Friday’s US data showed that University of Michigan sentiment fell from 48.1 in September to 46.30 (forecast 47.60), lowest since May, in its October preliminary reading. One-year inflation expectations rose from 4.6% to 4.7%, while five-ten-year expectations edged higher from 3.4% to 3.5%. Current conditions slumped sharply from 50.90 to 44.70 (forecast 50.10), a record low.NY Fed one-year consumers' inflation expectations rose to 3.90% in September — the highest since May 2023.The US trade deficit in August increased to its highest level since March 2025 as imports hit a record high of $420.80 billion.Indian Rupee strengthened Monday as the RBI took extraordinary measures on October 10 to support the ailing domestic currency. These steps include to open a special window to meet state-run oil companies’ requirements, asking banks to park cash with the RBI for some forex transactions (equivalent of 20% of the notional amount of each derivative transaction exceeding $2 million), prohibiting dealers from re-booking cancelled forex derivatives involving the INR, and reduction in limits for forex derivative transactions without confirmed existence of the underlying assets to $5 million from $100 million.The US Dollar Index edged higher Monday as crude oil prices rose. The Index, at the time of writing, was hovering around 102.51, up nearly 0.25% for the day, as it approached the cycle high of 102.53, highest since April 10, 2025. The US bond market was closed to observe the ‘Columbus Day’ holiday.October Fed rate hike probability continues to fluctuate around 20%; in the last three weeks, the probability has fallen sharply from 70% following a weak non-farm payroll report for September and dovish Fed commentary.Markets see the Fed hiking rates three times by June 2027, though.The two-day Global Precious Metals Conference underscored the fundamental case for gold on central banks diversifying their reserves; geopolitical polarization and fragmentation reshaping the global monetary system; and rising concerns over sovereign debt.Participants see gold prices trading around $5,013.30 an ounce by this time next year.Hedge fund managers cut their net bullish god bets to 15-week low as they reduced their net-long positions by 9598 lots to 114,820 in the week ending October 6, according to weekly CFTC data.Long-only positions fell 4,411 lots to 130,247 in the week ending Oct. 6. The long-only total was the lowest in 16 weeks, while short-only positions rose 5,187 lots to 15,427 -- the highest in 10 weeks.Total known global ETF holdings slipped on October 9 to 101.12 Moz after rising for five days in a row. ETF investors sold 177,800 Ounces on October 9, most in 2 months. However, ETF holdings are up 2.17 Moz YTD after a huge turnaround in ETF flows since the cycle low of 96.16 MOz reached on July 20. Holdings are up ~0.20 Moz since the beginning of the Iran conflict on February 28.Registered COMEX inventory at 15.07 Moz, has remained nearly steady since September 30. It is down nearly 38% since the record peak of 24.25 MOz reached in April 2025.Speaking on economic outlook and monetary policy at National Association for Business Economics on October 12, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, a Fed hawk, said business pricing power and a sturdy economy show that interest rates are not high enough to tame inflation. She added that frequent and smaller rate increases are preferred over big rate hikes to allow businesses to adjust.Major US data on cards this week include weekly ADP employment change (October 13), September CPI inflation (October 14), September retail sales (October 15), Philadelphia Fed Business outlook (October 15) and September PPI inflation (October 15).Focus will be on Germany's and France's CPI data, too, which will be released on October 13 and October 15, respectively.UK's monthly GDP data will be released on October 15.Investors will pay attention to speeches of a battery of Fed speakers lined up in near term. The list of the Fed speakers includes Collins, Hammack, Waller, Barkin, and Bowman.The Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will participate in a fireside chat with IMF MD Georgieva at IMF's annual gathering on October 16 in Bangkok, Thailand.Healthy ETF inflows and reduced Fed rate hike support the shiny metal; however, strong risk appetite, surging oil prices, elevated yields, and high probability of Fed rate hike in the coming months continue to pressurize the metal.Going ahead, focus will be mainly on Warsh’s talk and US CPI data.In the very short term, gold may push higher, but upside is likely to be contained unless some other major fundamental factor crops up in the picture/oil prices fall sharply. Oil could be a tug of war between the US and Iran as November 3midterm elections approach.Support is at 4150/4100/$4000, while resistance is seen at 4225/4255/4280/4337.Trading the range (buying the dips/selling into rallies) with a suitable and tight stop-loss is advisable presently. It is to be noted that domestic gold prices are expected to be under additional pressure due to the possibility of the domestic currency strengthening further on the RBI’s measures.
Article Summary: Gold prices may rise in the short-term but the upside is likely to be capped, says Praveen Singh, Head Currencies and Commodities, Mirae Asset ShareKhan. Trading the range with a suitable and tight stop-loss is advisable presently.

Article Title: Oil prices hold near $105 per barrel as Trump eases sanctions on Russian fuel
Article Text:
Crude holds near $105 per barrel

Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday after rising by nearly $2 a barrel in the previous session, as traders weighed the risks to supplies from attacks on Saudi Arabia against the prospect of additional diesel supplies from Russia.West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was trading at $92.84 a barrel, down $0.90, or 0.96%, while Brent crude fell $1.01, or 0.95%, to $105.60 a barrel. This comes after Brent futures had settled at $106.65 a barrel on Monday, their highest level since September 15.Oil markets have found some relief after US President Donald Trump said that Russia has agreed to supply diesel to global markets. The US administation temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel, which were designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war on Ukraine.These additional supplies could ease tightness in global fuel markets and temper some of the supply concerns that have supported crude prices in recent weeks.However, lawmakers from both parties in the US complained that Trump's agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin appeared to violate US law barring imports of Russian energy until Moscow ends its aggression against Ukraine.Concerns about the vulnerability of energy infrastructure and shipping lanes in the Gulf continued to weigh on market sentiment after Iran-aligned Houthis struck Riyadh's international airport over the weekend.Attacks on tankers were also reported near the Strait of Hormuz.The incidents threatened to derail the recovery in Middle East supplies seen in September, reinforcing concerns about further disruptions along one of the world's most important energy transit routes.Ministers of OPEC and non-OPEC Participating Countries in the Declaration of Cooperation said shipping and insurance costs had surged to unprecedented levels, exceeding one-third of the commodity value. The higher costs were impeding the efficient movement of crude oil and petroleum products.OPEC has also lowered its forecast for oil demand growth this year to 400,000 barrels per day (bpd), from 1.4 million bpd at the start of the year, reflecting developments throughout the year, the organisation's secretary general, Haitham Al Ghais, said on Monday, as cited by Reuters.Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs said that brent crude prices could fall to the $60s per barrel in 2027 if oil production in the Persian Gulf recovers faster than expected. However, the investment bank warned that further escalation in the region could push prices significantly higher.The bank said Brent could decline to the $60s if average oil output in the Gulf in 2027 rises by 1 million bpd above February 2026 levels.“A faster recovery in Mideast output and/or a faster erosion of the risk premium are the most likely potential triggers of price downside,” Goldman Sachs said.Continued adjustments in Middle East oil supplies would eventually bring crude prices down but renewed escalation in the region remained a significant risk that could push prices higher.Now, the Middle East conflict has continued disrupt energy supplies for over seven months now, rattling oil markets and pushing prices high. However, even with the ongoing tensions, the spike is far lower than the $126 per barrel seen earlier during the crisis.
Article Summary: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was trading at $92.84 a barrel, down $0.90. Brent crude fell $1.01, or 0.95%, to $105.60 a barrel. Brent futures had settled at $106.65 a barrel on Monday, their highest level since September 15.

Article Title: RBI measures see sharp impact as rupee rises 1% against US dollar; what steps were announced?
Article Text:
The rupee has recovered sharply following the RBI's announcement.

RBI announces measures for rupee

The rupee gained a stunning 1% at the start of trading on Monday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) eased pressure on the currency by shifting oil companies' dollar purchases away from the spot market and taking steps to curb corporate demand for forward dollars.The rupee began Monday’s session at 95.76 against the US dollar, compared with its Friday closing level of 96.73.In fact, it emerged as one of Asia's strongest-performing currencies, even as most regional currencies moved within a narrow range. Despite Monday's sharp rise, the rupee has lost 6.6% against the dollar so far this year, according to a Reuters report.Also Read | RBI has record forex reserves, but why is rupee still not out of the woods?On Saturday, the RBI announced a set of measures targeting two major sources of pressure on the rupee. These include sustained dollar purchases by oil marketing companies amid elevated crude prices and demand from corporates looking to protect themselves against further currency depreciation.Fears of additional weakness in the rupee had prompted importers to increase their purchases of forward dollars to shield themselves from potentially higher costs in the future.However, the increased demand for hedging also put further pressure on the currency.This created a cycle in which expectations of depreciation encouraged more hedging, adding to the rupee's weakness and reinforcing those expectations.Among the measures announced by the RBI were a ban on companies rebooking cancelled rupee-linked derivatives, a reduction in the threshold for transactions that do not have an underlying exposure, and a requirement for banks to maintain a 20% cash reserve against certain foreign-exchange contracts. These steps could make hedging against a weaker rupee more expensive.Citi said in a note that the package increases the immediate cost of trades aimed at benefiting from rupee depreciation.Bankers clarified that the restrictions do not cover every foreign-exchange transaction and apply only to current account transactions.The 20% cash requirement also excludes companies hedging external commercial borrowings and foreign portfolio investors seeking to hedge their investments in India.The rupee has recovered sharply following the RBI's announcement, but analysts believe the durability of the gains will depend on whether the underlying pressures on the currency begin to ease."Beyond the initial impact, the rupee’s trajectory will continue to be shaped by crude oil prices, foreign portfolio flows and the broader direction of the US dollar," Societe Generale said in a note.
Article Summary: The rupee gained a stunning 1% at the start of trading on Monday. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) eased pressure on the currency by shifting oil companies' dollar purchases away from the spot market. The rupee began Monday’s session at 95.76 against the US dollar, compared with its Friday closing level of 96.73.

Article Title: India's economic story in fast lane, IMF projects 7% GDP growth for FY27 and FY28
Article Text:
India's growth story remains strong

India holds its ground despite higher oil prices

World Bank, OECD raise India growth forecasts

Global growth faces a more fragile outlook

India’s economy is expected to grow by 7% in both 2026 and 2027, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), keeping the country among the fastest-growing major economies despite growing uncertainties. According to the institution, strong domestic demand, robust services activity and favourable demographic trends are expected to support this growth.India's growth prospects were supported by favourable demographic dynamics, a large and expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms, even as higher oil prices posed a challenge.“India stands out with upward revisions, reflecting sustained momentum and growing evidence of stronger growth potential supported by favorable demographic dynamics, a large and expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms.”The forecast comes amid a series of upgrades by global agencies after India's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 7.8% in the April-June quarter of the current financial year.The agency expects India to remain among the fastest-growing major economies, with domestic demand and services activity helping sustain momentum.“India remains among the fastest-growing major economies, with growth in 2026 projected at 7.0 percent.This reflects stronger-than-expected momentum, supported by resilient domestic demand and robust services activity.”It also highlighted how the Indian economy continued to expand despite rising oil prices. “India’s growth remained robust, underpinned by domestic demand and services, despite higher oil prices.”The improved outlook follows the stronger-than-expected GDP growth recorded in the April-June quarter, prompting several global institutions, including the World Bank, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), S&P Global Ratings, Moody's Ratings, Fitch Ratings and the Asian Development Bank (ADB), to raise their growth estimates for India.The World Bank raised its growth projection for India in 2026-27 to 7.1%, from 6.6% estimated earlier. The multilateral agency attributed the revision to strong domestic demand and exports, despite global headwinds. It expects the economy to grow by 7.2% in 2027-28.The OECD has also increased its forecast for India's GDP growth in 2026-27 to 7.1%, from 6.3% projected in June. The revised estimate is higher than the 7% forecasts from S&P, Moody's and ADB, while Fitch expects growth of 6.9%.Moody's Ratings raised its forecast for India's real GDP growth in FY27 to 7%, from 6%, citing the economy's resilience amid the Middle East conflict."Although we continue to expect India to grow faster than all other G-20 economies, as well as similarly rated emerging market sovereigns, risks remain," Moody’s said.Expansion in the April-June quarter was supported by strong investment and manufacturing activity, which helped offset weakness in mining and consumer-facing services.While India has received a series of growth upgrades, the IMF has warned that the global economy's resilience is becoming increasingly fragile and uneven.“The global economy remains resilient, but that resilience is becoming more fragile and more uneven. Growth is projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, while inflation is expected to reach 4.7%, driven largely by higher energy and food prices.”The global outlook also presents risks for India.Higher crude oil and energy prices could fuel inflation and put pressure on household purchasing power. Below-normal monsoon rainfall could affect agricultural output and rural demand, while prolonged geopolitical tensions could disrupt supply chains and increase input costs.Despite the upward revisions to India's growth projections, these factors remain among the risks flagged by agencies assessing the country's economic outlook.
Article Summary: India's economy is expected to grow by 7% in both 2026 and 2027. Strong domestic demand, robust services activity and favourable demographic trends are expected to support this growth. The IMF has warned that the global economy's resilience is becoming increasingly fragile and uneven.

Article Title: Man worked in South Korea and received salary in US dollars in NRE account, income tax department sent notice; ITAT Bangalore sets aside assessment and orders fresh review
Article Text:
On September 23, 2026, the ITAT Bangalore ruled in his favour and granted him relief. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the man win the case in ITAT?

As a non-resident Indian are you liable to pay tax in India? In one such case, the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Bangalore, has granted relief to an employee who received a tax notice over salary payments made by his foreign employer to his Non-Resident External (NRE) bank account in India.A man from Karnataka moved to South Korea to work for a company that had won a major project from Samsung Heavy Industries in South Korea.Under the arrangement between Samsung Heavy Industries and Ocean Rig UDW Inc., the man was required to work at Samsung's shipyard from September 2014 to June 30, 2016.Also Read | Man invested Rs 10 lakh, which tax department treated as unexplained; he first cited cash loan, then bank withdrawals as source, ITAT Nagpur deletes addition and Rs 2.11 lakh penalty His responsibility was to supervise the construction of a vessel. His employment contract reflected these terms, specifying his designation as a supervisor and stating that he would work as an electrician at the project site in South Korea, according to an ET report based on the claims made in the judgement. His salary was fixed in US dollars and transferred directly to his NRE account in India.The arrangement, however, came under scrutiny when the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) in Bangalore issued a tax notice. The AO pointed out that the man’s NRE account had received salary credits in US dollars and concluded that he was employed by a foreign company.The AO further noted that the man had neither filed foreign tax returns nor submitted a copy of his Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), despite working for an overseas employer.On this basis, the officer included his salary income in his total taxable income. The AO also added the difference in the interest income received, making the man liable to pay income tax on the salary credited to his NRE account.The draft assessment order also recorded that the man had not disclosed the salary income in his Indian income tax return (ITR).The Dispute Resolution Panel (DRP) upheld the AO's position and dismissed the man’s objections. It cited his failure to provide the TRC, foreign tax returns and evidence of tax payments in Congo. The DRP also held that salary paid by an employer into a bank account in India is deemed to accrue or arise in India and is therefore taxable in the country.Challenging these findings, the man approached the ITAT Bangalore.On September 23, 2026, the ITAT Bangalore ruled in his favour and granted him relief.Also Read | Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemption ITAT Bangalore noted that the bank statements submitted by the man supported his account of the transactions. It also observed that the entries in his passport established his non-resident status during the relevant period. In view of these findings, the tribunal held that the question of taxing the salary income he received did not arise.The tribunal further clarified that whether the man had paid tax in the foreign country could not, by itself, determine whether his income was taxable in India.It pointed out that the AO had disregarded the passport and bank statements furnished by the man solely because he had not submitted other documents, including foreign tax returns, a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and details of taxes paid abroad.The ITAT Bangalore did not agree with this approach. It held that the AO's conclusion was not correct when the man had been able to establish that he was a non-resident during the relevant assessment period.The tribunal said: “The NRE account also establishes the fact that the assessee had received the salary in USD. In such circumstances, the assessment order passed by the AO is not in accordance with the provisions of the Act.”ITAT Bangalore also held that the man’s failure to furnish the foreign tax returns, TRC and details of taxes paid abroad could not be the sole reason for rejecting his claim, given that the available evidence established his non-resident status and showed that he had earned the salary in US dollars.Also Read | Grandmother and her son gifted 2.5-acre land to his second wife, who sold it; his daughter from first marriage claimed it was ancestral, but Madras HC rejects her plea Accordingly, the tribunal set aside the assessment order passed by the AO and sent the matter back to the officer for fresh adjudication.It directed the AO to examine the man’s passport entries and NRE account records and decide the issue on the basis of these documents, without insisting on copies of his foreign tax returns, the TRC or proof of tax payments in the foreign country.Karanjot Singh Khurana, Partner at DMD Advocates, told ET that for the assessment year 2016-17, the man filed his income tax return (ITR), in which he was assessed as a non-resident.ITAT Bangalore noted that the man had already furnished evidence establishing the facts relevant to determining his tax liability in India. His passport entries and NRE bank statements showed that he was a non-resident during the relevant assessment year. On the basis of these facts, Khurana explained that the man’s foreign salary was not taxable in India, irrespective of whether he could produce a TRC or demonstrate that he had paid tax in another country.However, the ITAT Bangalore did not conclude the reassessment proceedings itself. It set aside the reassessment order and sent the matter back to the Assessing Officer for fresh consideration. The AO was directed to decide the matter on the basis of the man’s passport entries and NRE bank account records, without insisting on the TRC, foreign tax return or details of taxes paid in the foreign country.Also Read | Son claimed share in mother’s Delhi house, saying he paid Rs 1.5 lakh for land and Rs 60,000 for construction; Delhi High Court rejects claim, orders him and wife to vacate
Article Summary: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Bangalore, has granted relief to an employee who received a tax notice over salary payments made by his foreign employer to his Non-Resident External (NRE) bank account in India. A man from Karnataka moved to South Korea to work for a company that had won a major project from Samsung Heavy Industries in South Korea. On September 23, 2026, the ITAT Bangalore ruled in his favour and granted him relief.

Article Title: Gold jewellery gets costlier as prices surge 54%; shoppers turn to Rs 10,000-Rs 1 lakh diamond pieces, as jewellers use 18-carat, 14-carat and 9-carat gold to make it more accessible
Article Text:
Jewellers are also turning to 18-carat, 14-carat and 9-carat gold.

Gold prices rise, diamonds are back in focus

Gold prices have risen sharply from levels seen in last year’s festive season. The sharp hike in gold prices is prompting jewellery buyers to consider diamonds as an alternative, with retailers projecting a 15-20% increase in diamond jewellery sales this festive season.Retailers said the Navratri season has begun on a strong footing for studded jewellery, as shoppers look for pieces that offer value while staying within their budgets. The trend points to a broader change in consumer preferences, with diamond purchases increasingly driven by personal choices and everyday use instead of being limited to weddings and other special occasions.As gold jewellery becomes more expensive, shoppers are increasingly exploring diamond-studded ornaments priced between Rs 10,000 and Rs 1 lakh.Also Read | Gold at Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams is pushing middle-class Indian buyers to silver who are getting 650 grams of silver at the same price; some betting silver at Rs 2.3 lakh per kg may hit Rs 4 lakh Jewellers are also turning to 18-carat, 14-carat and 9-carat gold for these pieces to keep them within reach of a wider range of buyers. This allows consumers to opt for lighter jewellery without having to compromise on design.Smaller diamonds have become more affordable, making studded jewellery an appealing option for consumers looking to avoid the higher cost of gold ornaments. Prices of small diamonds are around 25% lower than during the 2025 festive season, while gold prices have climbed 54% over the same period."Diamond jewellery sales have witnessed an uptick at Joyalukkas because it fits the budget of consumers as lower caratage gold is used," Joy Alukkas, chairman of pan-India jewellery retail chain Joyalukkas told ET."We are expecting a growth of 20% in diamond jewellery this festive season. However, competition in the retail jewellery space is hotting up as many regional players are expanding their footprint and entering the equity markets with their IPOs."Demand for diamond jewellery meant for everyday use is also picking up. Senco Gold & Diamonds expects sales in this category to rise 20% this festive season. "Earrings, rings, pendants and bracelets in the price range of Rs 30,000-Rs 1 lakh are showing fast movement," said Suvankar Sen, managing director at Senco Gold & Diamonds.Consumers are also changing the way they shop for jewellery, turning to lighter pieces as elevated gold prices push up the cost of traditional ornaments."Even at Rs 25,000, one can get diamond jewellery," Ishu Datwani, founder of Mumbai-based Anmol Jewellers, told the financial daily. "Moreover, the look-to-price ratio of diamond jewellery is much higher. Customers are preferring lightweight gold jewellery now. Earlier, if they bought a necklace weighing 100 grams, they are now settling for 60 grams."The shift is particularly noticeable in the Rs 10,000-Rs 1 lakh segment, where buyers are finding fewer options in gold jewellery. "There is hardly any good gold jewellery in the Rs 10,000-Rs 1 lakh price bracket," said Colin Shah, managing director of Kama Jewelry. "So, consumers are preferring diamond jewellery. Smaller stones have become popular in this price range."Also Read | Unscrupulous jewellers may use fake stamps to mark your gold: As hallmarking charges rise to Rs 75 from Rs 45 Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council flags risk of rise in fraudsters Demand is also growing for modern diamond jewellery designs that can be worn regularly, rather than being reserved for weddings or other special occasions."With gold prices at elevated levels, we expect diamond jewellery to see increased interest this festive season," said Supriya Kataria, founder of Kumari Fine Jewellery. "Consumers are increasingly looking for pieces that offer distinctive design, versatility and the flexibility to be styled beyond a single occasion." Kataria expects demand for diamond jewellery to increase by 15-20% this festive season.
Article Summary: Gold prices have risen sharply from levels seen in last year’s festive season. The sharp hike in gold prices is prompting jewellery buyers to consider diamonds as an alternative. As gold jewellery becomes more expensive, shoppers are increasingly exploring diamond-studded ornaments.

Article Title: MDR on UPI transactions over Rs 2,000 deferred; to come into effect post Diwali
Article Text:
Govt defers 0.4% merchant discount rate on UPI payments

MUMBAI: Its official. There will be no MDR on UPI until the festival season is over. The National Payment’s Corporation of India’s The UPI and Services Steering Committee has deferred the implementation of merchant discount rates (MDR) on select person-to-merchant UPI transactions until immediately after Diwali, citing the festive season. The implementation date will be notified separately.The Times of India had reported last week that finance ministry and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) have decided to defer the introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions, seeking to avoid adding to business costs and hitting consumption at a time of economic headwinds, people aware of the matter said. The revised rollout was expected to be pushed to January 2027 from October 15. However,the announcement on Tuesday states that the implementation will be immediately after Diwali.The MDR framework was approved and notified by NPCI on September 15, with a 0.4% charge for eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. The framework was to take effect from October 15, giving banks, payment aggregators and other ecosystem participants a month to make operational changes.ALSO READ: Pakistan angle under probe? Delhi Police files 4 FIRs over fake posts since Oct 10 The decision to defer the rollout comes just days before the scheduled start and follows demands from trade bodies and merchant associations for a January implementation. They have argued that introducing the fee during the festive season, when retail activity and digital payments typically rise, could increase costs for merchants and weigh on sales.The framework was designed to create a revenue stream for the payments ecosystem after more than six years of effectively zero MDR on UPI. The government had said the levy would apply only to specified merchant transactions, with payments up to Rs 2,000 and eligible small merchants continuing to remain free. About 96% of P2M transactions were expected to remain unaffected.The deferment gives merchants and payment companies more time to prepare while allowing the government to avoid introducing a new transaction cost at a potentially sensitive point for consumption.
Article Summary: There will be no MDR on UPI until the festival season is over. The revised rollout was expected to be pushed to January 2027 from October 15. The announcement on Tuesday states that the implementation will be immediately after Diwali. The decision to defer the rollout comes just days before the scheduled start.

Article Title: Tata chief flags challenges in India's semiconductor push, calls 'global collaboration a necessity'
Article Text:
Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran

'We need to also see where the demand is'

India has the potential to become a significant player in the global semiconductor supply chain, but investments must be guided by demand, financial viability and the ability to execute projects, Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran said on Tuesday.Chandrasekaran said that semiconductors would be fundamental to the country's future and meeting its domestic consumption requirements. He added that India's talent pool, the size of its domestic market and its potential to participate in international supply chains put it in a favourable position."We are in a beautiful spot in India, because we have the talent, we have the domestic market, we can play a part in every global supply chain," he said at the 2026 Bloomberg New Economy Forum.Chandrasekaran also highlighted collaboration with global players as a necessity to build the country's semiconductor ecosystem. Access to technology and the availability of energy would also be important considerations as India develops its manufacturing capabilities."We need partnerships, because we have all the technologies ... But if you design it, definitely we will get there. But you also have to be careful, because you need to keep an eye on energy," he said.Tata Electronics is setting up a fabrication plant in Dholera, Gujarat, with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC) as its partner. The project involves an investment of around Rs 91,000 crore and will manufacture chips for automobiles, mobile devices, consumer electronics, artificial intelligence and other industrial applications. Alongside, the group is developing a semiconductor assembly and test facility in Assam at an investment of around Rs 27,000 crore.The projects are intended to cater to rising domestic demand, reinforce India's semiconductor supply chain and strengthen the country's integration with the global electronics manufacturing ecosystem.Chandrasekaran cautioned that India and businesses should not rush into manufacturing the most advanced chips without first determining whether there was sufficient demand to justify the investment."You cannot be reckless and say that I am going to be putting a 2 nanometre chip (plant). It's just not going to work. So, we need to also see where the demand is," he said.He emphasised that financial viability was a key consideration not only for businesses but also for India and its people. Investments, he said, needed to make commercial sense and support sustainable employment over the long term."And the financially viable thing, you have got to see the sun cross the river," said Chandrasekaran, who was recently given a third five-year term as Tata Sons Chairman amid a boardroom tussle over the group's future.His comments come as the group pursues semiconductor investments while weighing the practical considerations involved in developing the sector. Although the long-term need for semiconductor capabilities is clear, decisions on the scale of investment, the pace of expansion and the technologies to be used remain important considerations.Chandrasekaran acknowledged that businesses operating in the global environment could not expect every aspect of an investment to be predictable. However, he said some fundamental factors remained certain, including energy requirements and the ability to execute projects."But a lot of things are certain. Energy is certain, the game is certain, the ability to execute is certain. And the only thing is how much you ramp up, how fast you ramp up, which technology you go to...," he said.
Article Summary: Chandrasekaran said that semiconductors would be fundamental to the country's future. He added that India's talent pool, the size of its domestic market and its potential to participate in international supply chains put it in a favourable position. Tata Electronics is setting up a fabrication plant in Dholera, Gujarat, with a partner.

Article Title: Power generation up 11% y-o-y in Q2: CREA
Article Text:
India’s electricity generation rose 11% year-on-year (AI-generated image)

NEW DELHI: India’s electricity generation rose 11% year-on-year to 536 billion units (BU) in the second quarter of 2026-27, while peak power demand touched a record 270 GW, 18% higher than the peak recorded in the corresponding period last year.Despite the surge in demand, coal-fired power plants were not operating at full capacity, pointing to significant headroom in the existing fleet even as renewable generation continued to expand, according to a report by Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).Renewable electricity generation, excluding large hydropower, crossed 100 BU for the first time in a quarter. Solar generation rose 39% year-on-year to 51 BU, while wind generation increased 29% to 45 BU. Solar accounted for 10% of total electricity generation for the first time, setting a daily record of 705 million units (MU) on Sept 30.Combined generation from non-fossil sources, including renewables, large hydropower and nuclear, reached a record 177 BU, up from 163 BU a year earlier. Thermal power continued to dominate the generation mix, accounting for 64% of total electricity generation.Coal-fired power plant utilisation fell to 68% in Q2 from 73% in the first quarter, while coal despatches to power plants declined from 74 million tonnes in May to 66 million tonnes in Aug, the lowest level recorded in 2026.CREA said the figures indicated that the coal fleet had substantial unused capacity even during periods of record electricity demand.Large hydropower generation rose to 60 BU from 39 BU in the first quarter, but remained 20% below the year-earlier level, as deficient rainfall amid El Niño conditions led to a shortfall.India’s installed power capacity stood at 555 GW in Aug, with non-fossil sources accounting for around 55% of capacity. CREA said the pipeline of battery and pumped-hydro storage projects had reached around 290 GWh, though only 9.1 GWh was operational.“As solar increasingly meets daytime electricity demand and storage helps meet evening and night-time peaks, new thermal capacity should be assessed against expected demand, renewable generation and storage availability. This will help avoid building capacity that could remain underutilised as India’s power system evolves,” said Manoj Kumar, India analyst at CREA.
Article Summary: India’s electricity generation rose 11% year-on-year to 536 billion units (BU) in the second quarter of 2026-27. Peak power demand touched a record 270 GW, 18% higher than the peak recorded in the corresponding period last year. Solar accounted for 10% of total electricity generation for the first time.

Article Title: 'Power to empower': PM Modi stresses need to make tech progress accessible to all
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi described India as the "mother of democracy".

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday called for technology, data, knowledge and innovation to be used to empower people and create opportunities for millions, saying the real question was not who possessed power but how it was used.PM Modi said India’s approach should focus on enabling people, promoting collaboration and helping others succeed rather than concentrating on control or competition.“Today, technology is power, data is power, knowledge is power, and innovation is power. But, the real question is not who has the power, but how it is being used. Will technology advance only a few people or create new opportunities for millions? Will knowledge remain the strength of a select few or enhance everyone's capabilities? This is where a new idea is born: power to empower. Moving beyond power to control, we need power to enable. Moving beyond power to compete, we need power to collaborate. And moving beyond power to succeed, we need power to help others succeed,” the Prime Minister added. He made these remarks while addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi.PM Modi said the principle of using knowledge, wealth and power for a larger purpose was rooted in India's traditions.“This is not new to India. We have always emphasised the importance of utilisation of knowledge, money, and power. The real value of power lies in its purpose,” he said.“Whoever possesses knowledge, wealth, and power, how they use it is crucial. The true value of power lies in its purpose, and it's crucial to understand this philosophy in today's times... Our thousands of years of tradition have taught us this, and in India, we have demonstrated its application in our governance and work culture,” he added.The Prime Minister also described India as the “mother of democracy” and said the country was focused on making technology more accessible to people across regions and economic backgrounds.“India focussed on making mobile data affordable, even students from small cities can have access to digital learning,” he said.PM Modi also underlined India's approach to global economic growth, saying, “We do not grow at anyone's cost, we grow with and for the world.”The Prime Minister said the government's role should be to strengthen citizens rather than make them dependent on the system.“The government has authority, but its purpose should not be to make its citizens dependent on the system. Rather, its purpose should be to strengthen and empower its citizens, and India is on this path. Following this path, India has lifted 250 million people out of poverty in the last ten years – more than the population of many countries in the world,” he said.Modi also cited the AI Impact Summit held in India, saying discussions had explored how artificial intelligence could benefit both people and animals.“AI Impact Summit was held in India, and Bloomberg also praised it highly. In this summit, alongside utilizing AI for humanity, how animals can benefit from AI was also made a topic of discussion... This demonstrates that the more capable India becomes, the more beneficial it is for humanity and the world,” he said.Welcoming the decision to host the forum in India for the first time, PM Modi said Bloomberg founder Michael Bloomberg had chosen the right place at the right time.“Every year at this forum, we discuss economy, energy, etc. For the first time, it’s been held in India. I’d like to say to Mr. Bloomberg that he has chosen the right place at the right time,” he said.The eighth edition of the Bloomberg New Economy Forum brought together more than 500 public- and private-sector leaders from around the world. Held under the theme “A World in Play: Defining the New Levers of Power,” the forum focused on shifting geopolitical dynamics, emerging risks and opportunities, and ways to support future economic growth.In a message ahead of the event, PM Modi said India was moving beyond being an investment destination to becoming a partner in shaping the global economy.“Today, India stands at a defining moment in its journey. India is no longer just a destination for investment; it is a trusted partner in shaping the global future. In our pursuit of Viksit Bharat (Developed India), we are working to build one of the most reliable growth engines of the world and a balanced world economic order,” he said.He added that the forum would give participants an opportunity to experience a country that was “not just participating in the new economy, but actively defining it.”
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for technology, data, knowledge and innovation to be used to empower people. He made these remarks while addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. PM Modi said the principle of using knowledge, wealth and power for a larger purpose was rooted in India's traditions.

Article Title: Rupee extends winning streak, rises to 94.96 against dollar as RBI tightens forex rules
Article Text:
Rupee jumps to 95 per dollar

RBI moves, Dalal Street and more in focus

Rupee extended its winning streak on Tuesday, strengthening to 94.96 against the US dollar. The currency opened at 95.53 in the interbank market and rose 82 paise or 0.7% from its previous close. The latest gains come after rupee's sharp rally on Monday, when it rose 93 paise to close at 95.78 against the dollar, clocking its biggest single-day gain in more than six months.The currency's recovery is attributed to a series of steps taken by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to ease immediate dollar demand and restrict excessive positions in the foreign exchange market. Forex traders expect these measures to reduce demand for dollars in the spot market and limit speculative bets against the rupee.Among the steps announced by the central bank are a dedicated dollar window for oil marketing companies through designated banks and higher costs for certain foreign exchange hedging transactions."With the RBI's measures supporting the rupee, we expect USD/INR to move towards 95.00–94.80 range in the near term," CR Forex Advisors MD Amit Pabari told PTI.The central bank announced tighter rules for foreign exchange derivatives on Saturday as part of its efforts to curb speculative positions against rupee.Banks have also been asked to set aside a 20% reserve for dollar purchases exceeding $2 million.Separately, the RBI directed authorised dealers (AD) not to allow users to rebook cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts involving the rupee. The restriction applies to both deliverable and non-deliverable contracts.The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of six currencies, slipped 0.15% to 102.43.Oil prices also moved lower, with Brent crude futures, the global oil benchmark, falling 1.11% to $105.47 per barrel.Alongside a stronger rupee, Dalal Street was also trading higher on Tuesday. BSE Sensex gained over 600 points to reach 72,584.50, while NSE Nifty advanced 200 points to 22,575.30.Foreign institutional investors, however, continued to sell equities. According to exchange data, FIIs were net sellers to the tune of Rs 1,708.48 crore on Monday.Separately, government data released on Monday showed that retail inflation rose sharply to 5.54% in September, largely on account of higher onion and other food prices. The increase, however, kept inflation within the RBI's tolerance band.
Article Summary: Rupee rises to 94.96 against the US dollar on Tuesday. Currency's recovery attributed to steps taken by the Reserve Bank of India. BSE Sensex gains over 600 points to reach 72,584.50, while NSE Nifty advanced 200 points to 22,575.30.

Article Title: Tenant claimed landlords withheld Rs 10 lakh security deposit and refused to vacate shop; Delhi High Court rules against him, orders payout for unauthorised stay
Article Text:
When the 2018 rent agreement expired in 2019, the landlords asked the tenant to vacate. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about:

Why did the tenant lose the case?

Whether as a tenant or as a landlord, a proper paper trail is important to avoid disputes in future, and even if they do arise to prove your claim. In a recent ruling, the court asked the tenant to vacate and also pay for what was ruled to be an unauthorised stay.On September 28, 2026, the Delhi High Court directed the tenant to vacate the premises and pay mesne profits to the landlords for the period during which he continued to occupy the shop without authorisation.The case involved a tenant, who rented a 238.38 sq. ft shop in 2014 from a couple in Delhi. The agreed monthly rent was Rs 25,500. However, the 11-month rent agreement was never registered.Also Read | Landlords wanted tenant out to open a law office; he said the reason for seeking eviction had changed and other properties were available, why Delhi High Court upheld eviction The tenant subsequently claimed that he had paid the landlords Rs 10 lakh in cash as a security deposit between November 2016 and March 2017. However, he could not produce a receipt or any other documentary evidence to establish that the payment had been made.The tenant also told the court that rent agreements had been signed in 2015 at the same monthly rent and another agreement was executed in 2017. According to him, all these unregistered agreements had been prepared by the landlord couple.The dispute escalated in 2018, when another rent agreement was signed.The landlords maintained that the new agreement increased the monthly rent to Rs 29,000. Like the earlier agreements, this one was also unregistered and covered a period of 11 months.Although the tenant acknowledged that a fresh agreement had been executed in 2018, he disputed the claimed increase in rent. He argued that the monthly rent had actually been fixed at Rs 2,900, rather than Rs 29,000, because he had already paid a security deposit of Rs 10 lakh in the preceding years. The landlord couple firmly rejected his contention.When the 2018 rent agreement expired in 2019, the landlords asked the tenant to vacate the shop and hand over possession. The tenant, however, refused to leave unless his claimed security deposit of Rs 10 lakh was returned. The disagreement eventually developed into a legal dispute that reached the Delhi High Court.Also Read | Woman buys Rs 1.03 crore 3BHK in Bengaluru, but builder fails to provide specially-enabled parking; Karnataka RERA orders provision within 60 days and audited maintenance accounts The Delhi High Court noted that the tenant’s defence was based on his claim that he had paid the landlords Rs 10 lakh as a security deposit between November 2016 and 2017 in exchange for the shop. He maintained that, following this arrangement, he regularly paid monthly rent of Rs 2,900. The landlady, however, disputed his version and insisted that the rent was Rs 29,000 per month, not Rs 2,900.During her deposition before the District Court, the landlady stated that the monthly rent under the first agreement in 2014 was Rs 25,500 and that it had increased to Rs 29,000 in 2018. She also said that these details were reflected in her income tax return (ITR), according to an ET report.Her statement before the Delhi High Court was different. She said the tenant wanted to avoid paying GST and income tax, which was why the rent was collected in cash without issuing receipts. She further admitted before the High Court that she had not reported this rental income to the tax authorities.The landlord couple produced the 2018 rent agreement before the court. The tenant initially disputed the document, alleging that his signature on it had been forged and that the agreement was fabricated. However, he later acknowledged before the Delhi High Court that the 2018 rent agreement had been executed. This admission was inconsistent with his earlier denial, the ET report said.Also Read | Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemption When the tenant’s mother appeared before the court as a witness, she stated that the shop had been rented in 2014 at a monthly rent of Rs 25,500. She also denied having issued any receipt or paid Rs 4.5 lakh, which was supposedly part of the total Rs 10 lakh security deposit mentioned in her affidavit.Her testimony raised doubts about the tenant’s claim that he had paid the landlords Rs 10 lakh as a security deposit. In particular, the Delhi High Court took note of the fact that his own mother denied the payment of Rs 4.5 lakh referred to in her affidavit.The court further observed that the tenant had not shown that he attempted to record the alleged Rs 10 lakh arrangement in the rent agreements executed in 2016, 2017 and 2018. None of these agreements had been produced as evidence to substantiate his claim.As a result, the tenant failed to establish that he had paid the claimed Rs 10 lakh security deposit.Saumya Brajmohan, Partner at Solomon & Co, told ET that the tenant’s own statements weakened his defence, while he failed to produce evidence to support the key claims on which his case rested.In particular, he could not establish that he had paid Rs 10 lakh under a mortgage or security deposit arrangement, or that this payment had led to a reduction in the monthly rent to Rs 2,900.Another setback for the tenant was his failure to produce the rent agreements that he had acknowledged signing. He was also unable to demonstrate that any of these agreements documented the alleged Rs 10 lakh mortgage or security arrangement.Brajmohan says: "In other words, Mendiratta (tenant’s) fundamental problem was evidentiary: his pleadings, his cross-examination, and the evidence he led did not establish the alternative version of the tenancy that he relied upon.”The court found that his continued occupation of the shop after the tenancy ended up as being unauthorised and directed him to pay mesne profits for the period during which he remained in possession.Also Read | Sisters sought share in parents’ properties under Hindu Succession law; Madras HC rules for brother over mother’s land on ouster, father’s estate over missing parties
Article Summary: The case involved a tenant, who rented a 238.38 sq. ft shop in 2014 from a couple in Delhi. The agreed monthly rent was Rs 25,500. However, the 11-month rent agreement was never registered. When the 2018 rent agreement expired in 2019, the landlords asked the tenant to vacate. The tenant refused to leave unless his claimed security deposit of Rs 10 lakh was returned.

Article Title: Swarovski’s India growth shines as more consumers spend on themselves
Article Text:
Kolja Kiofsky, Chief Commercial Officer (CCO) at Swarovski

MUMBAI: With more Indians spending on themselves and widening their jewellery collection beyond gold, growth for Austrian brand Swarovski is finding new sheen in the country, over two decades since its launch here. India is among the fastest growing markets for the maker of crystal jewellery, watches and accessories this year alongside Japan and the US, said global chief commercial officer Kolja Kiofsky. “India as a market in the past was very occasion and gifting driven. While gifting is still very important, self-purchases are growing at a higher rate. In the past, the split between gifting and self purchases would have been around 80-20 (%) but now it is getting closer to 50-50. The Indian consumer market has really evolved significantly,” Kiofsky said in an interview.Swarovski has a play in the accessible luxury market, a space that has seen an entry of new shoppers on the back of higher disposable incomes. Some of its products across watches and jewellery at the entry level, for instance, are priced between Rs 13,000-25,000. The brand’s fastest growing consumer cohort in India are those born post 1990–millennials in their early 30s and well into their second or third jobs.Having different pricing tiers has worked for the brand and it will double down on this strategy, Kiofsky said, adding that the brand’s design and craftsmanship is what sets it apart from competitors in a crowded local market. “Our products are a reward for hard work, it is feeling good about yourself…..not really a daily necessity. Our jewellery lends to experimenting and expressing one’s personality…here’s an opportunity beyond gold and cultural relevance,” Kiofsky said.India’s luxury market is driven by a strong appetite for jewellery, analysts at Kearney said in a report published last year. “Jewellery and watches are Indian consumers’ favourite luxury segments, and their popularity has grown as displays of affluence are becoming more accepted…..moreover, India’s lower cost of living compared with Western countries means that discretionary spending starts at lower income levels,” analysts at the firm said, estimating the broader luxury market to touch $12 billion in revenues by 2028 from $7.7 billion in 2023.With the bulk of its sales coming from brick-and-mortar outlets, Swarovski will open new stores in India, besides being open to exploring new delivery formats, Kiofsky said. The brand expects to record a bigger Diwali season this year. “We don’t believe that there’s a slowdown to the (consumption) trend we have seen year-to-date. Our LFL growth has been showing double-digits,” Kiofsky added. The company also expanded its offerings in the market with the launch of lab-grown diamonds in 2024.
Article Summary: Swarovski has a play in the accessible luxury market. The brand’s fastest growing consumer cohort in India are those born post 1990. The company also expanded its offerings in the market with the launch of lab-grown diamonds in 2024.

Article Title: HCLTech Q2 YoY revenue up 2.2% to $3.7 billion, narrows FY27 guidance
Article Text:
The company’s services business grew 3% sequentially, generating more than $100 million in incremental revenue

Mumbai:

HCLTech’s dollar revenue rose to $3.7 billion in the September quarter, up 2% sequentially and 2.2% year on year. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 2.3% sequentially and 2.6% year on year. EBIT margin expanded 131 basis points sequentially and 71 basis points year on year to 18.2%.The company’s services business grew 3% sequentially, generating more than $100 million in incremental revenue. About $50 million came from advanced AI and the remaining $50 million from the core business, where HCLTech is gaining market share through AI-driven services.HCLTech narrowed its FY27 company revenue growth guidance to 2.5%-4% in constant currency terms from the 1%-4% announced in Q1. Services revenue growth guidance was revised to 3%-4% from the earlier range of 1.5%-4.5%.CEO C Vijayakumar said the company retained the midpoint of both guidance ranges despite narrowing them, reflecting caution about extrapolating recent improvements in demand amid a volatile business environment.“Although we saw demand improve towards the end of the first quarter, we remained cautious because the business environment has been volatile over the past two years.We did not want to extrapolate recent positive developments too aggressively,” Vijayakumar said.He said client conversations had been encouraging, with enterprises focused on scaling AI adoption and delivering measurable business outcomes. Clients were also seeking ways to extend AI-driven productivity gains across software development and IT operations, where benefits demonstrated in smaller projects had proved harder to replicate across entire organisations.Vijayakumar said it was too early to call an industry-wide inflection point, though HCLTech expected FY27 to be better than the current year. The company will review its guidance after the third quarter. Its data centre investments are expected to contribute meaningfully from the second half of FY28, given the long gestation period of such projects.Advanced AI revenue, which includes AI factories, physical AI, agentic AI and AI advisory services, reached $219 million in the quarter, equivalent to an annualised run rate of about $876 million. It grew 28.4% sequentially and 78% year on year in constant currency terms.“Advanced AI should deliver higher margins than our existing business,” Vijayakumar said, adding that the company would reinvest gains to strengthen its AI capabilities and gain market share.CFO Shiv Walia said HCLTech retained its EBIT margin guidance of 17.5%-18.5% despite acquisition-related costs. “Despite these costs, we retained the margin range by absorbing the impact,” he said, referring to amortisation and transition services costs.HCLTech’s global workforce stood at about 2.3 lakh at the end of the Sept quarter, after increasing by 6,450 employees during the period. This represented quarterly growth of 2.9% and annualised headcount growth of 1.6%.The company added 6,136 freshers during the quarter, about 1,000 more than in the year-ago period. Around 15% were in its elite engineer category. HCLTech expects to hire about 10,000 freshers for the full year.On the US govt’s suspension of permanent labour certification processing, HCLTech CHRO Ramachandran Sundararajan said: “The number of PERM applications we have filed over the past couple of years has been very small. Therefore, we do not expect the suspension to have any material impact on our workforce plans or client engagements.”
Article Summary: HCLTech’s dollar revenue rose to $3.7 billion in the September quarter. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 2.3% sequentially and 2.6% year on year. EBIT margin expanded 131 basis points sequentially to 18.2%. CEO C Vijayakumar said it was too early to call an industry-wide inflection point.

Article Title: Manipur on edge after fresh killings; 9 killed in 12 hours, shutdowns disrupt key highways
Article Text:
CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh condemned the killings of civilians and appealed for restraint and dialogue.





GUWAHATI: Manipur ’s hill districts remained tense on Sunday after nine people were killed in 12 hours of ethnic violence across Kamjong, Kangpokpi and Ukhrul districts on Saturday.Additional security forces were deployed in the affected areas of Kangpokpi and Kamjong districts, while separate shutdowns disrupted traffic on National Highways 2 and 202.The Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) called a 24-hour strike from Saturday evening. The Kuki CSOs Working Committee, Ukhrul, also enforced a shutdown in Ukhrul over the killings and its allegations of involvement by Naga militants and security personnel. No fresh fatality was reported on Sunday.CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh condemned the killings of civilians and appealed for restraint and dialogue. “CM has instructed the authorities concerned to take immediate and effective steps to tackle the situation, restore peace and order, and ensure the safety and security of all citizens,” the CM’s office said.The Kuki Chiefs’ Association, Manipur (KCA-M), on Sunday condemned what it called a “pre-planned attack” on unarmed civilian protesters in Chassad Kuki village in Kamjong district on Oct 9 and 10. It alleged that cadres of the NSCN (I-M), NSCN (Eastern Flank) and ZUF-K, in collusion with Tangkhul IRB personnel posted in the district, carried out the attack.“In this cowardly attack, the armed groups opened fire on civilian protesters and burnt down houses in Chassad village, resulting in the killing of Domkhonei Touthang and Michael Ngamminlen Haokip, both innocent Kuki civilians of Chassad village, and the destruction of houses,” the KCA-M said in a statement.The association claimed that the latest incidents took the number of Kuki civilian victims killed in attacks allegedly led by Tangkhul-led NSCN groups since March 11 this year to 30.The KCA-M demanded the immediate registration of FIRs for murder, arson and criminal conspiracy against the alleged perpetrators and the “involved IRB personnel”, along with their arrest. It also sought ex gratia payments of Rs 30 lakh each and govt jobs for the next of kin of the deceased, besides full compensation and the urgent reconstruction of the burnt houses.“Centre and security forces must understand the ground reality and secure all Kuki villages in Kamjong, Ukhrul, Tamenglong and Noney districts with adequate deployment of central forces to prevent further attacks,” the KCA-M said. It reiterated its demand for a separate union territory with a legislature for the Kuki-Zo people under the Constitution, saying this was necessary for lasting peace and security.The 12-hour outbreak of violence claimed six Naga lives, two Kuki lives — including that of a mother of five — and the life of a Gorkha farmer. Gunfights and arson targeting homes and shops were reported across the three districts, marking one of Manipur’s deadliest outbreaks of violence in the past year.Meanwhile, the working committee of the Tangkhul Naga Long (TNL), the apex traditional body of the Tangkhul Naga community, condemned the attacks on Tangkhul Naga civilians and alleged repeated aggression against border villages in Kamjong.“The external aggression against the border Naga villagers of Kamjong by the Kuki war parties has become a routine affair since the outbreak of violent conflict in the hills of Manipur,” it said.“In spite of the grim and alarming situation along the India-Myanmar border, the current political dispensation at Imphal and New Delhi has become a helpless spectator to the cross-border terrorism, while wilfully leaving their innocent citizens at the mercy of the foreign aggressors,” the organisation alleged.The TNL urged the authorities to take measures to protect residents living along Kamjong district’s porous international border.
Article Summary: Nine people were killed in 12 hours of ethnic violence across Kamjong, Kangpokpi and Ukhrul districts on Saturday. The 12-hour outbreak of violence claimed six Naga lives, two Kuki lives — including that of a mother of five — and the life of a Gorkha farmer.

Article Title: Gandhinagar civic polls: BJP wins 38 of 44 seats, Congress gets 5

Article Title: Dow rises, S&P 500 near record as Wall Street braces for key US data
Article Text:
Wall Street opened the week on a mixed note, with energy stocks gaining

Wall Street stocks traded mixed on Monday, with the S&P 500 holding near its record high as gains in energy shares offset losses in technology stocks. Investors also turned their attention to a fresh round of corporate earnings and key US inflation data due later this week.The S&P 500 rose 0.1%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.4%, adding 228 points. The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.2%, reflecting pressure on some of the technology stocks that have helped drive the market's gains this year.Energy shares advanced as crude oil prices climbed amid concerns over global supplies. Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose 2% to $106.77 per barrel. Oil prices have fluctuated sharply in recent weeks amid uncertainty surrounding the US war with Iran and its implications for energy supplies and inflation. Chevron gained 1.4%.Technology stocks were among the biggest drags on the market, with Micron Technology falling 2.8% and Advanced Micro Devices declining 2.4%. Investors are looking for evidence that the surge in artificial intelligence-related investment will translate into sustained earnings growth and justify the sector's strong stock-market performance.Artificial intelligence continues to support the outlook for technology companies and their suppliers, but questions remain over the longer-term returns from the technology.As companies begin reporting quarterly results, investors will be watching whether earnings can sustain the momentum behind market valuations.Oil prices remain another key variable for markets. Rising crude costs can push up petrol and diesel prices, increase transportation expenses and feed into the cost of goods. This could complicate the Federal Reserve's efforts to bring inflation down to its 2% target.Investors will get fresh readings on price pressures and consumer demand this week. The US consumer price index (CPI), due on Wednesday, is expected to show annual inflation rising to 3.6% in September from 3.4% in August. Producer price inflation and retail sales data are scheduled for Thursday, offering further insight into business costs and household spending.The data could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decisions. Persistent inflation has kept the prospect of further rate increases in focus, while higher bond yields have raised borrowing costs across the economy. The 10-year US Treasury yield recently touched its highest level since 2002 before easing to 5.24% late Friday. US bond markets were closed on Monday for the Columbus Day holiday.The housing market will also be in focus, as elevated mortgage rates weigh on affordability and demand. Investors are due to receive an update on home sales on Tuesday.Meanwhile, the latest earnings season gathers pace with results from major US banks. Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo are scheduled to report on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America on Wednesday. Their results are expected to provide clues about lending activity, consumer finances and the broader economic outlook.Elsewhere, European markets advanced, while most Asian markets ended lower. Tokyo markets were closed for a holiday.
Article Summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.1%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.4%. The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.2%, reflecting pressure on some of the technology stocks that have helped drive the market's gains this year. Energy shares advanced as crude oil prices climbed amid concerns over global supplies.

Article Title: Industrialised personalisation
Article Text:
Industrialised personalisation, in the world of service, means a system set down so completely that anyone properly trained can replicate it and make an experience feel personal.

You have been inside the hotel for less than a minute when the waiter at the restaurant door greets you by name. Your usual table, the one by the window, is already laid. Before you open the menu the waiter asks whether it will be the sole again, as it was in March, and you, who eat out a good deal and are hard to impress, feel for a moment like the only guest in the building. You have not said anything. The waiter takes your coat with a small bow and leads the way.In 1911, Frederick Winslow Taylor's ‘The Principles of Scientific Management’ held that the best way to do each job should be worked out in advance, and taught. He wrote, “In the past the man has been first; in the future the system must be first.” Industrial production could then continue seamlessly, with each new worker fitting into the role with ease.The same logic had already moved from products into service, from Fred Harvey's railway restaurants in 1876 to White Castle's hamburger stands in 1921, and in 1948 the McDonald brothers rebuilt their restaurant around a nine-item menu and ran the kitchen like an assembly line. Let's follow a new hire called Dan on his first morning at the McDonald's on Sand Lake Road in Orlando, the chain’s largest outlet. For a moment he is overwhelmed by the arcade, ordering kiosks and a sea of impatient customers.The hour of briefing he was given steadies him. He matches each order number to its table, carries the tray over and says, as taught, “Have a nice meal!” In under a day few can tell he is new. This is industrialised industrialisation, with systems in place but execution still a little rough around the edges.In time, Dan moves to a job at a formal dining room where he trains for a whole week. He moves more fluidly now, personal worries don’t reflect in his demeanour, and his ‘thank you’ with a smile and a gentle nod sounds less rehearsed. The management has done its work well, and it takes a trained eye to see that his manner at the next table is no different.Attention reaches further at Eleven Madison Park, where, Will Guidara has said, whoever greeted you would have looked you up online beforehand. In ‘Unreasonable Hospitality’ he describes training the staff to set every plate so that in the event that a guest turned it over, he’d find the Limoges stamp facing him, right side up.At the Ritz-Carlton, Joseph Michelli reports, guest relations staff share news of arriving guests' anniversaries and celebrations at the daily lineup. You could arrive on a special day and find champagne, a handwritten card and pastries waiting in the room. The Ritz keeps the record of such care in Mystique, a database of guest preferences fed by notes that staff are trained to jot down. If you stayed at one of its hotels, the waiter would likely have drawn on it.Industrialised personalisation, in the world of service, means a system set down so completely that anyone properly trained can replicate it and make an experience feel personal.Dan leads you to the window. When the sole comes, it is cooked the way it was in March.
Article Summary: In 1911, Frederick Winslow Taylor's ‘The Principles of Scientific Management’ held that the best way to do each job should be worked out in advance, and taught. Industrial production could then continue seamlessly, with each new worker fitting into the role with ease. Industrialised personalisation means a system set down so completely that anyone properly trained can replicate it.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Brent crude declines as Trump announces Russia-Ukraine energy truce
Article Text:
Russian diesel supplies ease market concerns.

Oil prices fell on Monday as expectations of additional Russian diesel supplies and a possible halt to attacks on energy facilities in the Russia-Ukraine conflict eased some concerns over supply. However, continued tensions in the Middle East kept Brent crude above $100 a barrel.Brent crude futures fell $1.54, or 1.47%, to $103.18 a barrel by 7.24 am IST. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude declined by the same amount, or 1.68%, to $90.31 a barrel.ICE gasoil futures, a benchmark for diesel, fell 3% to $1,436 per barrel after US President Donald Trump said Russia would supply additional diesel to US and global markets.Earlier on Friday, Trump said that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel, equivalent to around 2.25 million barrels.He added that another 500,000 tonnes would be supplied in November, followed by a further 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.Global daily diesel consumption is forecast to be close to 29 million barrels, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA).Trump also announced on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other’s energy facilities. However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he was still waiting for details of the proposed energy ceasefire.The announcements eased some immediate concerns over supply, said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade, Reuters reported.“Questions remain over the validity and longevity of any such ceasefire, and without clearer evidence that it will actually hold, the extent of the pullback is likely to stay limited,” he added.Despite the easing of some supply concerns, the conflict in the Middle East continued to support oil prices. The Houthis claimed responsibility for a Saturday strike on Riyadh's international airport that reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300.Saudi authorities also reported injuries in another attack on the airport on Sunday.Trump said on Saturday that the US was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.
